key_insight: Bag-of-waves learns a small, interpretable dictionary of EEG waveform atoms and uses token counts plus temporal/spatial extensions to classify EEG data effectively, even in low-data settings.
engineering_relevance: It offers a lightweight, label-free alternative to deep EEG models that can preserve interpretability while reducing data, compute, and parameter needs.
method: Learn shift-invariant k-means waveform atoms from unlabeled EEG
Convert continuous signals into atom tokens and n-gram transition counts
Extend to multichannel regional and cross-channel spatial atoms
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on three datasets spanning low-data mouse genotype clustering, resting-state dementia classification, and the six-class TUEV EEG event benchmark, with performance competitive with strong deep and foundation models.
watch_item: The approach depends on the quality and stability of learned atoms, so performance may vary with preprocessing choices, dictionary size, and how well the learned templates generalize across cohorts or recording setups.
paper_title: Interpretable EEG biomarkers with bag-of-waves: Spatial and temporal waveform dictionaries for low-data regimes
